chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who left his mother and his brother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sheikh, do you want (the ruling) based on the Book (Quran)?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the closest (relative), then the closest.' I said, 'So the brother does not inherit anything?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I have informed you that Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the closest (relative), then the closest.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits first, the mother or the brother, according to the practice of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'qurb' (proximity) in inheritance, where the Imam cites Ali ibn Abi Talib’s practice of distributing assets to the closest kin first. This establishes a practical precedence of the mother over the brother, illustrating how early Imamic tradition prioritized immediate familial bonds, a nuance that complements the fixed shares outlined in the Quran. It serves as a key reference for understanding the interplay between Quranic mandates and the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt in determining heir priority.
